title: SRE guard chronicle — night shift observations & follow-ups (2026-03-25)
content:
TL;DR: Night shift saw one medium-severity latency incident affecting p95 latency for hosted-inference small models; mitigated by rolling back runtime rollout; several noisy internal eval jobs amplified batching pressure; added immediate follow-ups, runbook notes, and short-term rate-limits for eval cluster. Overall system steady outside the window.

Shift summary (22:00 UTC -> 06:00 UTC):
- 22:05: routine bridge open, verified alerts baseline, no ongoing incidents.
- 00:48: spike in p95 latency for hosted-api-route /v1/generate-small observed across us-west-2 dedicated pools (p95 rose from ~140ms to ~420ms).
- 00:52: Pager: INC-4821 triggered (p95 > 300ms, error rate nominal).
- 01:10: Triage: identified concurrent rollout of runtime v1.12.4 to dedicated-az1; KV cache invalidations correlate with increased cold-cache misses.
- 01:28: Mitigation: rolled back dedicated-az1 to v1.12.3 (manual rollback via deployment manager), warmup script executed, cache hit rate returned to normal by 01:42.
- 02:00: Post-mortem notes started; incident declared medium severity; no customer-facing downtime.
- 03:15: Follow-up: internal evaluation jobs (internal-eval/*) spike discovered at 00:40–01:20 generating many single-token requests leading to suboptimal batching; added short-term rate-limit on internal evals at 03:30.
- 05:10: Routine checks, verified SLO dashboards and ingestion pipelines healthy.

Incident detail (INC-4821):
- Symptoms: p95 latency jump for small-model infer endpoints; throughput steady; error rate unchanged.
- Root cause hypothesis: rollout of runtime v1.12.4 introduced aggressive KV invalidation strategy for cache-aware routing that caused cold-cache windows per host during canary exposure. This combined with a burst of low-latency eval requests (high qps, small seq len) increased per-request overhead.
- Immediate mitigations applied:
  1) Rollback dedicated-az1 to v1.12.3 (01:28)
  2) Execute cache warmup: scripted prefix replay on primary hosts (01:33)
  3) Temporary rate-limit for internal-eval consumer (03:30)
- Observed outcome: p95 returned to baseline within ~15 minutes after warmup; no persistent errors.

Metrics & artifacts captured:
- Heap of perf traces: perf-traces/2026-03-25/INC-4821/*.span (see linked_artifacts)
- Cache hit ratio graph: dashboards/sre/kv-cache-hit/us-west-2 (spike window 00:40–01:40)
- Deployment audit: deploy-log/runtime/v1.12.4/2026-03-25-00:36

Runbook draft notes (to be merged into runtime-degraded-kv-cache runbook):
- Add explicit rollback checklist for partial AZ rollouts (steps + verification queries).
- Add manual warmup snippet (curl-based prefix replays and sample-corpus warmup).
- Add detection heuristic: simultaneous drop in KV cache hit ratio + p95 increase but stable 5xx indicates cache rollback vs model error.
- Add playbook: if rollout is <10% and incident appears within 30m, pause rollout and run warmup before continuing.
- Author note: need one-liner command for warmup that respects tenant isolation (avoid cross-tenant replay).

Follow-ups / Action items (owner, due):
- A: Update runtime rollout gating to include KV-hit sanity check (owner: Priya Kapoor, due: 2026-03-29).
- B: Enhance deploy alerting to surface cache-hit delta >10% within 15m (owner: Noah Patel, due: 2026-03-28).
- C: Add warmup utility to ops-toolbelt with tenant-safe mode (owner: eng-tools team / assignee TBD, due: 2026-04-05).
- D: Coordinate with Eval team to throttle internal-eval peak windows; propose scheduling window (owner: Emily Wu - eval team, suggested due: 2026-03-27).
- E: Draft post-incident writeup for engineering-all (owner: Liam Chen, due: 2026-03-26).

Notes to next shift: (to-sr/next)
- Verify the warmup tool execution logs for any residual cache fill failures: /var/log/ops/warmup-2026-03-25.log
- Check deployment manager: confirm no additional v1.12.4 rollouts pending in other AZs.
- Watch for recurrence pattern tied to small-seq-length requests; look at batching histogram and queue depth on serving runtime.
- Follow up on Jira JIRA-ENG-7580 (investigation ticket created) and comment on any additional traces you collect.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why did the rollout change the invalidation window size? (need patch-level diff from runtime team).
- Is there a way to pre-warm caches automatically during rollouts without tenant cross-talk?
- Can we detect eval-origin requests earlier to apply soft-throttles before they hit dedicated pools?

Misc notes / low-priority observations:
- Observed minor noise on EBS throughput for a single host during warmup — looks within normal variance but flagged it (SRE checkpoint).
- Suggest adding a short blurb in the on-call handbook about how to interpret KV-hit dashboards vs p95 spikes to reduce triage time for newer on-callers.

Appendix: quick commands used during shift:
- Rollback (deployment-manager): dm rollback runtime-service --az dedicated-az1 --to v1.12.3 --reason "INC-4821 KV invalidation"
- Warmup script (ops): ./ops/warmup/prefix_replay.sh --region us-west-2 --targets host-list-az1.txt --sample sample-corpus-small.json
- Quick cache hit check: curl -sS $DASHBOARD_API/kv-hit?region=us-west-2 | jq '.p95, .delta'

If anything in this doc is unclear ping me in #sre-oncall (PM me directly if urgent).

-- Liam
